question: Should the first denylist release be config-only, or should `exec-approvals.json` become a persisted denylist owner with an explicit mixed-version writer contract?
rationale: Omission currently means both “a new client intentionally cleared the list” and “an old client never knew the field,” so code cannot safely infer intent without choosing the permanent ownership and compatibility model.

options.title: Ship config-only first
options.body: Remove the persisted approvals-file/protocol denylist field for this release, retain `tools.exec.denylist` enforcement, and add UI-managed persistence later behind a versioned capability.

options.title: Version persisted policies
options.body: Keep both surfaces but add a protocol/file-version or capability contract that rejects or preserves unknown security fields and prove old-writer/new-host upgrade behavior.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Hold or close the PR until maintainers are ready to own the additional persisted policy and mixed-version support burden.

recommendation.title: Ship config-only first
recommendation.body: Remove the persisted approvals-file/protocol denylist field for this release, retain `tools.exec.denylist` enforcement, and add UI-managed persistence later behind a versioned capability.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and prior review routing connect steipete most directly to exec approval policy, release compatibility, and security-contract decisions.
